title: Penalty strategy against a goalkeeper: when to pick a side and when to watch

items.stem: Definitions: Which of these best defines the keeper-independent penalty strategy?

options.text: Aiming at the centre of the goal on every kick, whichever keeper you face
Fixing the target side before the run-up and not revisiting it
Waiting until the keeper moves, then kicking toward the opposite side
Picking the side at random on the final step of the run-up each time

items.stem: Definitions: Which of these best defines the keeper-dependent penalty strategy?

options.text: Choosing the target side before the run-up, using the keeper's habits seen on video
Kicking to the side the keeper dived to in the previous penalty he faced
Using the keeper's first movement during the run-up to pick the opposite side
Changing the speed of the run-up depending on how early the keeper starts to move

items.stem: Definitions: In penalty strategy, what does it mean to say a goalkeeper has "committed"?
Definitions: What does "mixing strategies" mean for a penalty taker?

options.text: Varying the pace of the run-up so the keeper cannot time the dive
Aiming at one corner during the run-up and another at contact
Taking half of your penalties with each foot, so the keeper cannot predict which foot you use
Switching between choosing the side in advance and choosing it after the keeper moves

items.stem: Definitions: In one phrase, what is an "expected scoring rate" for a penalty strategy?

Applying it: Video of the opposing keeper's last four penalties shows him standing still in the first, then moving toward a post while the kicker was still running up in the other three (left, right, left). When you watch him and choose your side late, you score 90% if he has already moved and 40% if he stands still. A corner picked before the run-up scores 70% against him whichever way he goes. Which plan gives you the best chance to beat him?

options.text: Choose late, after seeing whether he has moved
Choose your best corner before the run-up and keep it whatever he does
Choose a side by coin flip on the final step of the run-up
Choose the side opposite his most recent dive before the run-up

items.stem: Applying it: You have 20 minutes of daylight to practice before Saturday's match, and you cannot see the opposing keeper play beforehand. Which plan builds the most reliable penalty?

options.text: Practice reading a keeper's first movement, so you can aim away from wherever he goes
Practice switching your aim in mid-run so you can respond to the keeper's movement
Practice power first, since a harder shot is harder to save wherever it is placed
Practice one fixed corner and one run-up until the strike repeats

items.stem: Applying it: Ana picks a corner before each run-up and keeps it. Ben watches the keeper and chooses his side late. Over a season they face keepers who stand still until the ball is struck. Compared with Ana, what is the most likely result for Ben?

options.text: Ben gains the chance to punish a keeper's early dive
Ben loses power because his aim keeps changing
Ben gains nothing from watching and still pays for a late choice
Both score at the same rate, because a keeper who waits is equally easy to beat

items.stem: Applying it: Against a keeper who dives early on 3 of every 10 penalties and waits on the other 7, plan X, watching him, scores 85% when he dives early and 45% when he waits. Plan Y, a corner chosen before the run-up, scores 62% either way. Assume these figures already include any accuracy lost. By how many percentage points does the better plan's overall scoring chance exceed the other's?

Applying it: You planned the left corner. On your last step the keeper leans left, so you switch your aim to the right corner. Compared with a kick aimed right from the start, which part of the kick is most likely to suffer?

options.text: Power only, because the run-up is cut short
Accuracy, because there is less time to adjust the kicking action
Nothing, because a trained kicker redirects as precisely as a planned kick
Accuracy improves, because you now know where the keeper is leaning
